To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best estimator of coverage is the ratio of the number of observed faults to the number of injected faults, that this estimator should be used in all practical situations, that the estimator can be made unbiased by using a space partitioning strategy, and that the "no-reply"-problem can be overcome through a posteriori stratified estimation.

(1) sampling in the whole input space yields unbiased estimators for the fault coverage; (2) the stratified sampling technique is a viable alternative when a partition of the space is available and the fault coverage is not too high; and (3) the a posteriori stratified sampling allows the scope of the tests to be widened.

(1) the coverage of a system is the probability that the system is able to detect and recover from all faults, (2) the coverage can be estimated by sampling the input space and counting the faults that are detected and the faults that are not detected, and (3) the coverage can also be estimated by using a priori knowledge of the target system and the faults that can be injected in the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of estimating the fault tolerance coverage of a system by means of a limited set of fault injection tests, and with the problem of determining the minimum set of tests needed to obtain a reliable estimate of coverage.
the development of techniques to estimate fault tolerance coverage from fault-injection experiments.
the problem of estimating the effectiveness of fault tolerance mechanisms through the statistical processing of observations gathered in fault injection experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of fault coverage estimation is still open and that the techniques described in this paper represent a step towards its solution.
, for fault injection experiments, there are no universal estimators, but there are a variety of techniques that can be applied in different contexts.

the sampling techniques proposed in this paper allow the coverage of a given fault tolerance mechanism to be estimated in a statistically meaningful way, with an error bound that can be controlled and made as small as needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of estimating coverage is not a trivial problem and that the proposed techniques are useful to address it.

the coverage of a system is a function of its fault and activation models and that the coverage estimation problem can be solved with the help of statistical sampling techniques and a priori knowledge about the system.
the coverage estimators presented in this paper are useful in the context of the early stages of fault tolerance mechanism design and testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coverage estimation techniques are not a panacea.

the coverage of fault tolerance mechanisms is best estimated by using a sampling technique that exploits the structural information available about the system under test, and that the estimation process should start as soon as enough information has been gathered to allow the coverage of a significant fraction of the input space to be assessed.
, in order to obtain a reliable estimate of coverage, one should use a space partitioning technique, and the stratified estimator should be applied to account for missing classes in the space.
